body:
I verified example_fmri_effects() against your working tree while you have it open. It passes, and three numbers from that run are ready to drop into the vignette you are writing.

  mean total INSIDE  signal measurements   1.3314
  mean total OUTSIDE                      -0.0001
  argmax total is a signal measurement     TRUE

  inside    coherent 0.3606   configuration 0.9708
  outside   coherent -0.0000  configuration -0.0001

  54.8 percent of outside-region total estimates are below zero

The third one is the useful one. It independently reproduces the 52.4 percent I measured in a pure-null simulation, but from YOUR fixture rather than mine - which means the 'why negative values are not a bug' section can be written from example_fmri_effects() alone, in three lines, with no simulation code in the vignette. That policy is currently asserted in five places in the docs and demonstrated in none, and this closes it.

The middle pair is the other one worth using: a planted multivariate pattern reads configuration 0.97 against coherent 0.36 inside, and both essentially zero outside. That makes coherent-versus-configuration concrete in one table, which is the single most abstract thing in the framework.

Two design choices you made that are better than what I asked for, recorded so they do not get undone later: returning a FIT rather than a bare relation means the same fixture reaches the error-channel capabilities including rdm_sampling_covariance, and returning components that go straight into the workflow avoids the rMVPA anti-pattern where gen_sample_dataset returns a list users must unwrap and four vignettes re-wrap it wrongly.

Still open from my side and unaffected by this: the exact-equality assertion at introduction.Rmd:87, which I sent separately - identical() on total versus coherent + configuration, where the true residual is 1.4e-17.
